### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx`  _(via requiresConfirmation (symbol, a field of const object TOOL_RETIRED_KEY_GUIDANCE))_
- `content/docs/ai/tools.mdx`  _(via requiresConfirmation (symbol, a field of const object TOOL_RETIRED_KEY_GUIDANCE))_
- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/api/environment-routing.mdx`  _(via HttpDispatcher (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via HttpDispatcher (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via HttpDispatcher (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via HttpDispatcher (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx`  _(via requiresConfirmation (symbol, a field of const object TOOL_RETIRED_KEY_GUIDANCE))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via HttpDispatcher (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 25ee507651f7bae209771fb31661e6edf46f4c8f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a3b4491f5f960a936b9f2477b8a510fd5f2df6f8` — the merge of head `c34fcbc8386e5600b517596cc20c2fcc341ef472` into base `25ee507651f7bae209771fb31661e6edf46f4c8f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a3b4491f5f960a936b9f2477b8a510fd5f2df6f8 && git checkout a3b4491f5f960a936b9f2477b8a510fd5f2df6f8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 25ee507651f7bae209771fb31661e6edf46f4c8f c34fcbc8386e5600b517596cc20c2fcc341ef472 && git checkout -B drift-repro 25ee507651f7bae209771fb31661e6edf46f4c8f && git merge --no-ff c34fcbc8386e5600b517596cc20c2fcc341ef472

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 25ee507651f7bae209771fb31661e6edf46f4c8f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 25ee507651f7bae209771fb31661e6edf46f4c8f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6729ea847c8065d9389fad09aca4732186e4f57a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/tool.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/ai/tool-confirmation-prescription-tense.pin.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-confirmation-gate.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/mcp-resume-run.test.ts, packages/mcp/src/__tests__/stdio-agent-account.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/service-account-register-key.dogfood.test.ts; cited, read only: packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts, packages/runtime/src/index.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts, docs/adr/0151-ai-service-account-a-headless-agent-is-a-registered-principal-of-its-own.md, .github/workflows/ci.yml

Inputs read: PR #32926 (body, 2 comments, 13 files, net diff against `main`), PR #32691 (body, 2 comments), the check-runs on this head. Changeset and `content/docs/**` are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT` and are not judged sentence by sentence here.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Request accept set, narrowed for one caller class at four doors: right.** For an AI service account an action declaring `ai.requiresConfirmation: true` is refused at REST `/actions`, at a host's `dispatchAction` under `rest`, `ai` and no posture, at MCP `run_action` and at MCP `resume_run`, with the confirmation member and without it. This is ADR-0151 D3 rule 3 as written ("refused for an account, and never confirmed by the account itself").
- **Every other caller, unchanged: right.** The sequence asks the gate on `posture === 'ai' || isAiServiceAccountCaller(wiring.ec)`; a person, a delegated agent (`onBehalfOf` present), a missing envelope and the system context take the branch they took on `main`.
- **Who is an account: right.** `principalKind === 'agent'` with no `onBehalfOf` is the shape the shared assembler stamps for an `agent` row on every face (`assemble-execution-context.ts`: the account arm takes precedence over the OAuth arm and never sets `onBehalfOf`), and the spelling `dispatchFlowAction` and `domains/automation.ts` already read.
- **Wire answer: right.** Code, status and `details` are the registered `428` `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` with `ActionConfirmationRequiredDetails`; only `message` differs by caller. No new error code; the ledger row under `@objectstack/runtime` already covers REST `/actions` and the host door as emitters of that package.
- **Schema accept sets: none moves, right.** `ToolSchema` refuses `requiresConfirmation` as before; the hunk changes the rejection's prescription string and a comment. `ActionSchema` is untouched.
- **Package entry surface: none, right.** `packages/runtime/src/index.ts` exports `dispatchAction` and three types from `action-dispatch.ts`; the gate's fifth parameter and `isAiServiceAccountCaller` are module-level exports of `action-execution.ts`, not on the `exports` map.
- **Published contract prose beside the hit: not moved with the door, wrong.** See finding 1.
- **Gate verdicts.** Every check-run on this head concluded `success` or `skipped`; the skips are by event (`pull_request`). One of them bears on the diff: the three `Dogfood Regression Gate` shards are skipped on a pull request (`ci.yml`), and the bare `Dogfood Regression Gate` concluded `success` with no shard run, so the two new dogfood cases have no CI verdict on this head. The queue build runs them.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/runtime` patch and `@objectstack/spec` patch: right. Those are the two packages whose shipped source moves; `@objectstack/mcp` and the dogfood package change tests only.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, line-initial in the PR body and the changeset: right. Nothing widens and no entry export is added; the narrowing is real and breaking, and the changeset carries the BREAKING banner, the `!` title and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). `Check Changeset` concluded `success`.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. No key, value or metadata type changes. The authorable `action.ai.requiresConfirmation` keeps its declared meaning (`ui/action.zod.ts`: confirmation for AI invocations); the door now holds one more AI caller to it. Per AGENTS.md step 3 a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch`.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up #32936` is present, as a `(narrowing)` arm owes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **stdio pins an absence, not a refusal: accepted.** `wireBridgeTools` registers the action tools only on a bridge that carries `listActions` and `runAction`, and the case reads the bridge `bridgeDataTools` receives. See nit 4.
- **Dogfood scope (REST only, no audit service, no MCP plugin in the showcase boot): accepted.** "Nothing run, no record read, no invocation row" is pinned in the two runtime harnesses, whose read counter is shown live by a person's control. The dogfood cases themselves are unmeasured by this head's check-runs (① above).
- **Skills docs follow-up #32936: accepted as a follow-up, with two additions.** The file list in the PR body omits `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`, whose `run_action` description still reads "REFUSED unless you also send confirm: true" (nit 5). `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts` is not skills prose and cannot ride that follow-up (finding 1).
- **`http-dispatcher.ts` comment left as is: accepted.** Its "unless the request carries the confirmation member" is incomplete for an account and points at the gate's docblock, which carries the rule (nit 2).
- **Full dogfood battery "running" when the body was written:** not a verdict; the queue build is.
- **`open_questions`:** none stated in the PR body.
- **#32691:** its two comments are a claim with hand-over and the supersession note. No ruling and no earlier record to carry.
- **Author:** `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no separate-author note is owed.
- **Docs Drift Check (advisory):** of its three pages the diff touches one; the other two state no rule this diff moves on a grep-level read. The sentence check stays the lane seat's.
- **Escalated, not blocking:** the account's refusal is byte-identical in code, status and `details` to the retryable one, and at REST its `details.confirmationMember` names a member the REST body does not define. Whether a machine reader should be able to tell the two apart is a contract-shape decision (a `details` member or a code), for the maintainer or the hold door ADR-0151 names (O6).
- **Outside this diff's doors:** three observations are relayed to the security seat privately. None is a finding on this head.

### ④ Design judgment

**The schema hit, `tool.zod.ts`: holds.** The added sentence says an AI service account "is refused at every action door, REST `/actions` included, whatever its request carries". Read against the live tree: every action dispatch arm (`dispatchFlowAction`, `executeRegisteredAction`, `executeDeclarativeUpdateAction`, the api forward) is reached only through `runResolvedAction`, whose admission half asks the gate for an account under both postures; its two callers are the REST and host door (`runResolvedActionAsRest`) and `invokeBusinessAction`; `resume_run` asks the gate per candidate with the caller's envelope. "For a person's call" on the REST bound is true. First consumer, an author meeting the rejection: the text states the refusal, both bounds and the account rule, and denies nothing the door does. The pin anchors each half (the gate reads the caller, the member never attests for an account, the sequence's condition and its fifth argument, the prose sentence).

**Implementing files, against "an AI service account is refused a confirmation-gated action whatever it sends".**

- `action-execution.ts`: agrees. The declared flag is read first; for an account the member is never read; the refusal keeps code, status and `details`; a required fifth parameter means no door can omit the caller by default.
- `action-dispatch.ts`: agrees. The gate stays after the param contract and before the subject load, so a refusal reads no record, and the row is written only for an admitted call.
- `domains/mcp.ts`: agrees. `resumeAdmissionRefusal` hands `ec` to the gate for each candidate; every refusal precedes `resume()`.
- Tests: agree with the code. Account cases at REST, MCP, host (three postures, member and no member) and resume; controls for a person, a delegated agent, an ungated and a `false` action.

**Tried to break it.** A request member, a posture choice, a host call under `rest`, a resume of a parked run, an in-process `api` forward into `/actions` (a key caller's forward relays its own identity headers, so the REST door resolves the same account), an OAuth arm naming an account (the assembler's account arm wins), a missing `principalKind` (the assembler stamps it for an `agent` row on every face; a host door uses the envelope its host resolved, as `dispatchAction`'s contract states): each reaches the same gate with the account's envelope, or cannot arise.

**Findings.**

1. **should-fix.** `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts` is the published contract the hit cites as enforced ("`AIActionConfirmation`, `@objectstack/spec/contracts`"). Its JSDoc on `AIActionConfirmation` says a door "MUST refuse a call when, and only when" the flag is `true` "and the request does not carry the confirmation member as `true`", and that "a client that always confirms ... is always correct"; `ActionConfirmationRequiredDetails.confirmationMember` is "the request member the caller must set to `true` and retry". After this diff the door refuses an account whose request carries the member. The diff bumps `@objectstack/spec` and moves the door, and leaves the normative text behind; the pin reads one carrier (the `ToolSchema` rejection) and not this one. Fix: state the account rule in those two docblocks, regenerate any reference page that projects them, and add the carrier to the pin. Earns a delta review.
2. **nit.** Unqualified sentences left in edited or cited comments: `action-execution.ts` gate docblock ("the caller confirms and retries"; "A client that confirms whenever the listing says `true` is always correct"), `error-code-ledger.zod.ts` ("the identical call with the member set succeeds"), `http-dispatcher.ts` ("unless the request carries the confirmation member"). The new docblock section qualifies them.
3. **nit.** `tool.zod.ts` comment: "the REST carve-out is a person's alone". The sequence leaves REST outside the gate for a delegated agent too, as `action-dispatch.ts` says. The shipped string ("for a person's call") is true and silent on that caller.
4. **nit.** The stdio case's title states more than its assertions read: it asserts the seams of the one bridge `bridgeDataTools` receives. Narrow the title or widen the assertion.
5. **nit.** `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`: the `run_action` description teaches the retry to every caller, and an account's `list_actions` row for a gated action carries no `unavailable`. Add both to #32936.

One should-fix and four nits; no must-fix.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8e2c6ee48a0e46d1a86143f3dd58cb4ae478a3e0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/tool.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts + packages/spec/src/ai/tool-confirmation-prescription-tense.pin.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-confirmation-gate.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/mcp-resume-run.test.ts, packages/mcp/src/__tests__/stdio-agent-account.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/service-account-register-key.dogfood.test.ts; cited, read only: packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts, packages/runtime/src/index.ts, packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, .github/workflows/ci.yml

Delta review on record 6839924123 (head `6729ea847c8065d9389fad09aca4732186e4f57a`), same reviewer. Judged: the one commit between the two heads (7 files, comments, JSDoc, one pin case, one test title), the refreshed PR body, and the check-runs on this head. `main` is not re-merged. Everything record 6839924123 judged outside that commit stands unchanged. The `hits` grew by the two spec files the commit touches; both were read in the first round as cited files and are judged here as hits.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept sets and entry surface: unchanged, right.** The commit moves no executable line: comments in `action-execution.ts`, `http-dispatcher.ts`, `tool.zod.ts` and `error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, JSDoc on two exported interfaces in `contracts/ai-service.ts`, one new pin case and one test title. No schema, export, error code or runtime branch moves.
- **Published contract prose: now moved with the door, right.** See ④, finding 1.
- **No projection left behind: right.** No reference page under `content/docs/**` carries the changed JSDoc or the ledger comment; the retired sentences survive only in `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md`, which is history.
- **Gate verdicts on this head (read 2026-11-13T01:12Z).** No check-run has failed. Concluded `success`: 20, among them both `Check Changeset` runs, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build Docs`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Spec property liveness`. **Pending (`in_progress`):** `Build Core`, `Build UI Deps`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Live E2E UI`, `Test Core (1/8)` to `Test Core (8/8)`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · workspace`; their aggregates are not yet created. The new pin case therefore has no CI verdict yet; it is judged here by reading. The dogfood shards are skipped on a pull request as before, and the queue build runs them.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still right. The changeset is not in the commit. `@objectstack/spec` patch covers the JSDoc that ships in its declarations; `@objectstack/runtime` patch covers comment-only source; `@objectstack/mcp` changes a test title and publishes nothing. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and `Skills-docs: follow-up #32936` stand as judged.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **PR body, one stale note (prose face, the lane seat's):** the acceptance note still says the `http-dispatcher.ts` comment "is left as is", while this commit edits it and the body's own "The published contract" bullet says so.
- **Nit 5 of record 6839924123 (`mcp-http-tools.ts` description, `list_actions` row):** untouched by the commit, as routed. The PR body's follow-up file list still names two files and not that one; whether #32936 carries it cannot be read from this round's inputs.
- **Docs Drift Check (advisory):** grew to 11 pages because the commit touches `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` and `HttpDispatcher`; both touches are comment-only, so no page it lists can be falsified by them.
- **Escalation of record 6839924123 (a machine reader cannot tell the account's refusal from the retryable one):** still open, still not blocking. The new `confirmationMember` JSDoc now states the fact in prose.
- **Private relay of record 6839924123:** unchanged by this commit.

### ④ Design judgment

**Hits.**

- `contracts/ai-service.ts`: holds against the gate. "when, and only when" is gone; the added paragraph states the rule as the code runs it (an agent principal with no `onBehalfOf`, every action door, REST `/actions` included, the member not read, no retry succeeds). The always-confirming client is now a client acting for a person. `confirmationMember` says an account's refusal carries the member and that no retry of its own succeeds, which is what `actionConfirmationRefusal` answers.
- `error-code-ledger.zod.ts`: holds. The retry sentence is a person's caller's; the account sentence sits inside "an action whose AUTHOR declared" the flag, so it claims the declared case only.
- `tool.zod.ts`: holds. The comment now matches the sequence: the REST carve-out is every caller's but an account's.

**Implementing files.** `action-execution.ts` and `http-dispatcher.ts` comments agree with the gate, with the one imprecision in nit B. The pin case reads the right text: each slice runs from the docblock opening above the named interface to the named member, the positive match needs the rule sentence unbroken by a full stop, the length floor keeps the negative matches from passing on an empty read, and the two negative matches are the two retired sentences verbatim.

**Findings of record 6839924123.**

1. should-fix (contract prose, pin carrier, projections): **resolved.** Both docblocks state the rule, the pin reads them, and there was no projection to regenerate.
2. nit (unqualified retry sentences): **handled** in all three files.
3. nit (`tool.zod.ts` comment): **handled.**
4. nit (stdio case title): **handled**; the title now names what the case asserts. Its body comment keeps one wider sentence ("the account's tools are the bridge registered here"); no action owed.
5. nit: routed to #32936, see ③.

**New in this commit, both nits.**

- **A. nit.** `contracts/ai-service.ts`: "Every other caller is gated by the member as below" follows a sentence that names REST `/actions`. The docblock's frame is the AI-facing door, where the sentence is true; REST `/actions` is outside the gate for those callers, and the sentence would be exact with "at an AI-facing door".
- **B. nit.** `action-execution.ts` gate docblock: "(an AI service account is refused whatever it sends)" sits in a sentence about every action the listing reports `true`, which includes the undeclared heuristic case the gate does not refuse for anyone. The contract's wording, "refused a declared-gated action whatever it sends", is the exact one.

Two nits; no must-fix, no should-fix. Nits alone end the round.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · security#1 · head `8e2c6ee48a0e46d1a86143f3dd58cb4ae478a3e0`
